links.comparator_used: Raw FHIR JSON serialization (default format) vs. five alternative serialization strategies, including Narrative and Condensed
links.outcome: Downstream LLM quality on clinical QA, reasoning and summarization, measured by token-level F1 and LLM-as-judge clinical rubric score
links.effect: Condensed beat Raw JSON on F1 for 3/4 models (Wilcoxon p < 10^-17, N = 100), while Raw JSON scored higher on judge scores for 3/4 models (p < 10^-7). Narrative achieved 95% of Raw JSON's clinical quality at 83% fewer tokens. The Model x Serializer interaction was significant (Friedman p = 0.0009): GPT-5.4 favored Raw JSON, while Claude and the open-weight models favored compressed formats.
links.tradeoff: Raw JSON gave the highest judge-rated quality but used far more tokens. Narrative cut tokens by 83% with about a 5% quality loss. No universal best format exists, so the benchmark recommends model-aware serialization. Llama 3.1 70B failed on 100% of complex patients despite being within its nominal context window.
links.quote: The Pareto analysis resolves this tension: Narrative achieves 95% of Raw JSON’s clinical quality at 83% fewer tokens.

design_hint: FHIR serialization format selection and pre-deployment capacity verification
